Fitbit Edge is Google's slim, screen-based fitness tracker for active lifestyles and everyday wear. It has built-in GPS, over 50 workout modes, ECG, skin temperature, and up to seven days of battery per Google. It's Fitbit's first repairable tracker, with a replaceable battery. $179.99, pre-order now, on shelves Oct 27. Includes 3 months of Google Health Premium, which is needed for the Health Coach and Health Guardian.

Launch Team [...] Solution: The Edge is a tracker with a screen that stays slim and light. Per Google, the case is 11.5mm thick and 45% lighter than the Apple Watch Series 12. The Hybrid OLED display is Google's largest and brightest tracker screen yet, with 46% more viewing area than previous Fitbit trackers.

What makes it different:

 Battery: up to seven days on a charge, which is Google's figure from pre-production testing, so real results may be lower. Fast charging gives a full day of battery in five minutes with a 30W adapter, sold separately.
 Repairable: Google calls it Fitbit's first repairable fitness tracker, with a replaceable battery and modular internals.
 GPS: built-in GPS that works without your phone, with up to 40% better tracking accuracy than previous generations, per Google. [...] Launch Team

### Q: Do home fitness apps provide real-time form feedback using your phone camera?

Impakt: AI Coach & Super Health App can give real-time form feedback and rep counts using your phone camera — you need to keep the camera on while you exercise. The app's motion analysis and any workout highlight video are processed locally on the device, and clips are only uploaded if you choose to share them.

results.title: GitFit.AI: Track any nutrient, habit, or activity daily with AI | Product Hunt
results.content:
Hey there, ex-Blizz engineer of 2+ years. I recently left behind my stable career to improve my fitness and work on my personal projects. After about 4 months of hard work 4 weeks straight of using it myself, I'm finally confident to share it with you. For a little background, I am someone who tries to run 5 miles a day, optimize random nutrients I care about, and limit calories. I was annoyed with fitness / habit tracking. Every app wants to tell you what your goals should be. I don't need a coach. I have AI for that. And less coachy apps will still limit you in what you can track, and box in your data. So I made an app to fix that, which puts your daily habits, nutrients, and goals in one place, letting you track anything imaginable in simple grids, by simply snapping a pic of or typing [...] Subscribe
